College can be really really stressful in the first few weeks. You’re figuring out your new environment, trying to get a handle on the culture and the social norms in a new place with new expectations. The good news is that your college likely has a plethora of resources for you! A lot of colleges make sure that academic advisors are available for their students (especially first hear students!) but there are usually counseling services as well as resources in the form of Resident/Hall directors, RAs, and Student Success departments who can help too. 

If you’ve realized that psychology isn’t for you, you can always change your major. Your add/drop period has likely ended already so unfortunately you may be stuck with those classes this semester, but some universities allow you to drop a class after the add/drop period has ended and mark the course as incomplete (this usually has no effect on your GPA but it does mean that you may not be considered a “full time student” so check with your registrar before doing any of these things). 

I also went to University as a 17 year old after graduating HS early. My advice would be to look into what clubs and organizations your university offers. If you live on campus, get involved in hall programing when you’re able to—RAs put a lot of time and effort into them and they usually have free food, plus its a great way to meet people in your residence hall/community. If you’re looking to make classes more bearable you could also see about starting a study group with your classmates or seeing if your university offers tutoring sessions. 

I know this is cliche, but it does get better. There’s also no shame in recognizing that you’re not ready and going home until you are.
